q: Per the current IC 21/43 EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN/EGRESS procedure, what is step 1?
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – Off 2. Engine switch – Off 3. Fuel Shutoff Handle – Pull 4. Ejection Seats – Safe 5. Batt switches – Off.

q: Per IC 21/43 EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN/EGRESS, what is step 4?
expl: Current step 4 is Ejection Seats – Safe, then 5. Batt switches – Off. Older gouge (p.6 / Quizlet EP1 #22) lists 'Throttle OFF, Engine Switch OFF, Fuel Shutoff PULL, BATT OFF, Emergency Egress' with NO seats step — older gouge, differs.

q: Which sequence matches the current IC 21/43 EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN/EGRESS?
opts: Throttle Idle → Engine switch Off → Batt switches Off → Fuel Shutoff Handle Pull → Egress
Engine switch Off → Throttle Off → Fuel Shutoff Handle Pull → Battery switches Off → Egress
Throttle Off → Fuel Shutoff Handle Pull → Battery switches Off → Egress
Throttle Off → Engine switch Off → Fuel Shutoff Handle Pull → Ejection Seats Safe → Batt switches Off
expl: IC 21/43 order. Older gouge EP 11X (p.77) on-deck fire/TP HOT: Throttle Off, Fuel Shutoff Pull, Battery Off, Egress (no engine switch, no seats) — older gouge, differs.

q: FIRE warning light on the ground (with or without secondary indications). Per IC 21/43 you:
opts: Engine switch – Off only, then taxi clear
Transmit to tower, then shut down
Throttle – minimum for safe flight and check secondaries
expl: IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT – GROUND: 1. Execute emergency shutdown/egress. Gouge p.5 #11: FIRE light requires immediate shutdown on deck without secondary indications; p.60 #25: no comms in procedure.

q: TP HOT caution light on the deck. Per IC 21/43:
expl: IC 21/43 TP HOT CAUTION LIGHT – GROUND: execute emergency shutdown/egress. Gouge p.59 #7 / p.64 #13: same procedure as FIRE light on deck.

q: TP HOT caution light in flight (e.g., cruising at 15K). Per IC 21/43:
expl: IC 21/43 TP HOT – IN-FLIGHT: 1. Throttle – minimum for safe flight. Gouge p.5 #12 / Quizlet EP1 #12: 'Throttle idle (min safe flight)'.

q: The TP HOT light is a ___ light; the FIRE light is a ___ light.
expl: Gouge p.60 #26: TP HOT is a CAUTION light (yellow), not a WARNING light (red) — RTFQ.

q: TP HOT caution light firewire threshold vs. FIRE warning light threshold:
expl: Gouge p.37 / p.54 #123–125: FIRE and GTS FIRE = 300°C outside the container; TP HOT = 150°C.

q: GTS FIRE warning light IN FLIGHT. Per IC 21/43, step 1 is:
expl: IC 21/43 GTS FIRE WARNING LIGHT – IN-FLIGHT: 1. Engine switch – off. Gouge agrees (p.59 #12, p.65: 'Engine switch – Off' first).

q: GTS FIRE warning light ON THE GROUND. Per IC 21/43:
opts: Press the GTS button to clear the fire
Engine switch – Off, then continue taxi
expl: IC 21/43 GTS FIRE – GROUND: execute emergency shutdown/egress. Older gouge EP 11X p.76 #30 lists 'Engine switch – Off, Throttle – Off, Fuel Shutoff – Pull, Battery – Off, Egress' (engine switch first, no seats) — older gouge, differs.

q: Per the gouge (6X corrections), the GTS FIRE warning light illuminates because:
opts: There is an overtemperature condition in the GTS compartment
There is a fire in the GTS burner can
expl: Gouge p.62 (E): overtemperature in the GTS compartment (not a fire in the burner can). p.54 #124: temp outside GTS container exceeds 300°C.

q: If the FIRE light comes on and then goes out, the gouge says this means:
opts: Firewire temperature dropped below 300°C (fire out) — or burn-through
The TP HOT sensor has taken over
expl: Gouge p.3: 'if the fire light comes on then turns off = temp below 300 or burn through.' p.37: firewire must remain below 300°C for 45 sec for the light to go out. p.53 #113: check light/continuity.

q: Per IC 21/43, the first step of CLEAR ENGINE PROCEDURE / ABNORMAL START / TP FIRE ON SHUTDOWN is:
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – off. Gouge p.77 #36 and p.59 #11 (overspeed on start: Throttle Off, not Throttle Idle).

q: Engine fails to light off within 15 seconds after moving the throttle to IDLE. This is a:
expl: Quizlet EP1 #1 / gouge p.5 #1, p.62 (G); p.56 #168: wet start = FF rises normally but no EGT/RPM within 15 s of idle.

q: RPM stagnates around 45% while EGT continues to rise during start. This is a:
expl: Gouge p.4 / p.56 #168: hung start = RPM stuck ~45%, EGT rising.

q: Hot start (gouge definition):
opts: FF and RPM normal, but EGT rapidly to 550°C or to 570°C for more than 10 seconds
EGT exceeds 450°C at idle for 6 seconds in flight
expl: Gouge p.56 #168. Ground start limit 550°C (570°C max for 10 s), p.37/p.56.

q: Overspeed during engine start — first step:
expl: Gouge p.59 #11, p.65 'OVERSPEED START – THROTTLE OFF'; matches IC 21/43 Clear Engine step 1.

q: Per IC 21/43 ENGINE FAILURE: if below ___ AGL and below ___ KIAS, eject.
expl: IC 21/43: If below 1,500 feet AGL and airspeed below 180 KIAS: 1. Eject. Otherwise: 2. Execute airstart. Gouge p.4, p.7 #2, p.60 #18, p.74 #10.

q: You just flamed out at 1,000 ft AGL and 150 KIAS. You should:
expl: Below 1,500 ft AGL AND below 180 KIAS → Eject (IC 21/43 ENGINE FAILURE; Quizlet EP1 #8).

q: Per IC 21/43 AIRSTART, step 1 is:
expl: IC 21/43 AIRSTART: 1. Emergency oxygen green ring(s) – pull 2. Throttle – off, then simultaneously 3. GTS Start Button – Press and 4. Throttle – Idle. Older gouge EP 11X p.77 #33 starts with 'Throttle – Off' (no O2 step) — older gouge, differs. Quizlet EP2 #14 does include 'Pull Emerg. Oxygen actuator' first.

q: Per IC 21/43 AIRSTART, which two steps are performed simultaneously?
opts: Throttle – Off and Emergency oxygen green ring – pull
GTS Start Button – Press and Engine switch – Off
GTS Start Button – Press and Throttle – Idle
Engine switch – Start and Throttle – MRT
expl: Steps *3 and *4: GTS Start Button – Press / Throttle – Idle. (Older gouge says 'GTS – Press and Hold'.)

q: Per IC 21/43 AIRSTART, the airstart is considered unsuccessful if:
opts: No relight within 30 seconds after moving throttle to idle, or stabilized EGT exceeds limits
RPM fails to reach 45% within 45 seconds
No relight within 15 seconds after pressing GTS
expl: IC 21/43: If unsuccessful (no relight within 30 seconds after moving throttle to idle or stabilized EGT exceeds limits): 5. Throttle – off (allow 30 seconds to drain if practical).

q: Per IC 21/43 AIRSTART, you may repeat steps *3 and *4 if above:
expl: IC 21/43: If above 13% RPM and 250 KIAS, repeat steps *3 and *4. Gouge windmill airstart: <25K, 13% N2 min, 250 KIAS (p.7 #24, p.67, p.76 #26).

q: Windmill airstart envelope per the gouge:
opts: Below 15,000 ft MSL, less than 20% RPM
Below 25,000 ft MSL, minimum 13% N2, recommended 250 KIAS or greater
expl: Gouge p.58, p.67, p.73 #35, p.76 #26; Quizlet EP2 #24.

q: Assisted (GTS) airstart envelope per the gouge handwritten notes:
opts: Above 20,000 ft with more than 45% RPM
Below 25,000 ft MSL with at least 13% N2
Below 15,000 ft MSL with less than 20% RPM (GTS light on)
expl: Gouge p.58: ASSISTED – <15,000' MSL, <20% RPM – GTS LT ON. Immediate airstart: any altitude.

q: Which airstart has no altitude restriction (per the gouge)?
expl: Gouge p.60 #29, p.58: IMMEDIATE – ANY ALT.

q: Engine fire in flight (fire confirmed). Do you attempt an airstart?
opts: No — airstart is not performed for a fire
expl: Gouge p.61 'No airstart – FIRE in FLT'; p.65 'FIRE WARNING LIGHT – DO NOT DO AIRSTART'.

q: Compressor stall vs. flameout: for a compressor stall do you pull emergency O2 and perform an airstart?
opts: No — throttle idle first; airstart/emergency O2 are flameout actions
expl: Gouge p.65: STALL – first step Throttle – Idle; do you perform airstart – NO; pull emerg O2 – NO. FLAMEOUT – you do those first.

q: Audible bang/pops, EGT increasing, RPM decreasing indicate:
expl: Quizlet EP1 #2; gouge p.3, p.60 #17, p.61 (FF same).

q: Per IC 21/43 COMPRESSOR STALL OR EGT/RPM WARNING LIGHT, step 1 is:
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – idle 2. EGT/RPM – check.

q: Per IC 21/43 COMPRESSOR STALL OR EGT/RPM WARNING LIGHT, step 2 is:
expl: IC 21/43 step 2: EGT/RPM – check. Older gouge (p.59 #2, p.64 #7, Quizlet EP2 #18) 'Throttle Idle, Controls Neutralize, EGT/RPM Monitor' — older gouge, differs (no 'controls neutralize' step in the current list).

q: Per IC 21/43, after a compressor stall, if EGT is greater than 450°C for more than 6 seconds at idle you:
opts: Throttle – slowly advance to minimum for safe flight
expl: IC 21/43 step 3. Gouge p.54 #120: locked in stall = EGT over 450 for 6 seconds after selecting idle.

q: Per IC 21/43, after a compressor stall, if EGT responds normally you:
opts: Throttle – slowly advance to minimum for safe flight; minimize throttle movements
Keep throttle at idle and land immediately
expl: IC 21/43 steps 4–5.

q: The EGT/RPM warning light illuminates at:
Per IC 21/43 ABORT, step 2 is:
expl: IC 21/43 ABORT: 1. Throttle – idle 2. Speed brakes – extend 3. Brakes – apply 4. Hook – down (if required) 5. Brakes – release prior to crossing the arresting gear. Older gouge p.5 #9 / Quizlet EP1 #9 'BOARDS retract' — older gouge, differs (Quizlet EP2 #25 says 'extend').

q: Per IC 21/43 ABORT, the final step is:
opts: Hook – down 1,000 ft prior to the gear
Brakes – release prior to crossing the arresting gear
expl: IC 21/43 step 5. The gouge abort items stop at 'hook (1000 ft prior)'.

q: During an aborted takeoff with NO blown tire, the anti-skid switch should be:
opts: Left ON (do not turn anti-skid off)
expl: Gouge p.62 (C): for an aborted T/O (assuming no blown tire) DO NOT TURN ANTISKID OFF.

q: Per IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT on TAKEOFF, if fire is confirmed and you are unable to abort:
opts: Continue the takeoff and land as soon as possible
Execute emergency shutdown on the runway
expl: IC 21/43: If decision is made to stop: 1. Abort. If fire is confirmed and unable to abort: 2. Eject. Gouge p.60 #19, p.66 #21, p.74 #11.

q: Per the gouge, the first indication of a fire on takeoff is:
expl: Gouge p.3 and p.47 (TRUE).

q: Maximum abort speed is defined as the speed from which you can:
opts: Rotate and clear a 50 ft obstacle
Commence a stop on the remaining runway without using the overrun or arresting gear
expl: Aero gouge p.2 #33. (Aero notes: 'Max abort 125 – not 129'.)

q: Per IC 21/43 EMERGENCY CATAPULT FLYAWAY, steps 1 and 2 are:
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – MRT 2. Maintain 24 units AOA; if engine failed or unable to stop settle: 3. Eject. Gouge: 'throttle check full forward, 24 AOA'.

q: Engine failure during the catapult stroke. Per IC 21/43:
opts: Throttle – MRT and maintain 24 units AOA
expl: IC 21/43 EMERGENCY CATAPULT FLYAWAY: if engine failed or unable to stop settle – Eject. Gouge adds: if unable to eject, ditch straight ahead (p.5 #15, p.59 #6).

q: Per the gouge, ditching configuration is:
Launch bar warning light after a cat launch (per the gouge):
opts: Make an arrested landing aboard ship
Divert to a field and make a flared/minimum-descent-rate landing with the short-field arresting gear removed
Raise the gear to retract the launch bar
expl: Quizlet EP2 #29; gouge p.75 #20. p.72: L-BAR extended → land past arrest gear.

q: Launch bar actuation per the gouge systems notes:
opts: Extended (lowered) by HYD 1, retracted (raised) by a mechanical spring; electrically controlled
expl: Gouge p.3, p.54 #140 and hw correction p.60: electrically controlled, hydraulically extended, mechanically retracted. NOTE: Quizlet EP1 #14 / gouge p.5 #14 says 'mechanically extended, hydraulically retracted' — conflicts with the other gouge pages.

q: Per IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT IN-FLIGHT, step 1 is:
expl: IC 21/43 IN-FLIGHT: 1. Throttle – minimum for safe flight 2. Check for secondary indications of fire. Gouge p.60 #22 'first step is Throttle idle (min for safe flight)'.

q: Per IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT IN-FLIGHT, after checking for secondary indications, if fire is confirmed or flight control is lost:
opts: Throttle – off and Fuel Shutoff Handle – pull
expl: IC 21/43 step 3. Older gouge EP 11X p.76 #31 adds O2 pull, Throttle Off, Fuel Shutoff Pull, then eject / prepare for controlled ejection / flameout approach — older gouge, differs.

q: Per IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT IN-FLIGHT, if fire is NOT confirmed and control effectiveness remains:
opts: Throttle – off and prepare for flameout approach
expl: IC 21/43 step 4. The older gouge has no 'land as soon as possible' branch.

q: Secondary indications of an engine fire (per the gouge):
opts: Rising EGT, increased fuel flow (plus the FIRE light) — all of the above
expl: Gouge p.65: SECONDARY INDICATIONS OF FIRE: EGT ↑, FUEL FLOW ↑, FIRE LIGHT; p.59 #13 (startup: all of the above); p.47.

q: Cruising at 23K you get a FIRE light with secondary indications. Answer per the gouge/Quizlet (consistent with IC 21/43 'fire confirmed'):
expl: Quizlet EP1 #18 / gouge p.5 #18; IC 21/43: if fire confirmed – Eject.

q: Per IC 21/43 ELECTRICAL FIRE, the immediate action is:
expl: IC 21/43 ELECTRICAL FIRE: 1. Gen switch – off. Quizlet EP2 #3 matches.

q: Per IC 21/43 TOTAL ELECTRICAL FAILURE, the memory item is:
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Emergency oxygen green ring(s) – pull. Gouge EP 11X p.68/p.74 starts the same, then VMC, land as soon as practical, reset gen/batts, emergency gear, no-flap/no-slat arrested landing.

q: Total electrical failure: load shedding is:
expl: Gouge p.71 #28, p.74 #2, p.7 #26 / Quizlet EP2 #26: no load shedding (eliminates 3 of 4 answers).

q: Total electrical failure landing plan (gouge EP 11X):
opts: No-flap/no-slat approach and arrested landing (short-field trap recommended — no NWS)
expl: Gouge p.68 #2, p.74 #2; p.3: no emergency flaps with total electrical failure; p.51 #52: only the gear can be extended manually.

q: With a complete electrical failure, what can still be extended manually?
expl: Gouge p.51 #52 (False — only the gear).

q: First step for a GENERATOR warning light (gouge EP 11X):
expl: Gouge p.71 #16, p.75 #15a, Quizlet EP2 #30.

q: Generator failure indications:
opts: Master caution, tone, GEN warning light, loss of right MFD and HUD
Loss of all trim including primary stab trim
Loss of TACAN and both MFDs
expl: Gouge p.3, p.52 #72. TACAN remains (p.4).

q: To keep the left MFD powered during a generator failure:
expl: Gouge p.4, p.70/p.75 #15i; p.51 #58: LT MFD reverts to ADI, out after 2 minutes unless ORIDE.

q: With a generator failure (28 VDC generator bus lost), which trim remains?
expl: Gouge p.8 #35, p.76 #25, p.52 hw; p.55 #162: lose ail/rud/stby stab trim, trim indicators, HUD, RT MFD.

q: Battery endurance after generator failure:
opts: 27 minutes on two good batteries (12 minutes on one)
expl: Gouge p.51 #62.

q: Overvoltage unit takes the generator offline at:
expl: Gouge p.3, p.47 #14, p.51 #57; undervoltage unit deenergizes non-essential buses below 25 VDC.

q: Single AC inverter failure results in:
opts: AC INV caution light, tone, and loss of non-essential AC (VOR/ILS/MB/RADALT)
expl: Gouge p.3, p.31 #20, p.52 #64, #69; with one inverter failed you still have TACAN azimuth (p.52 #67).

q: With both inverters failed, what navigation is left?
expl: Gouge p.52 #68; p.69: DUAL FAIL → TCN azimuth lost.

q: AC INV caution light (per gouge/Quizlet EP2 #32):
expl: Gouge p.8 #32.

q: Approach idle function with total electrical failure:
expl: Gouge p.55 #163 (True).

q: CAUG (control augmentation) caution light in flight — you lose:
opts: ARI, SBI, yaw damper, and rudder trim

q: The CONTR AUG caution light illuminates when:
opts: The system is degraded, a BIT test is in progress, or the paddle switch has been depressed
expl: Gouge p.41; p.61 hw 'CAUG Illum – FAILURE, BIT TEST, PADDLE OFF'.

q: CAUG BIT requirements:
opts: Weight on wheels, less than 80 knots, flaps/slats up

q: Trim-failure exam question answer (gouge):
expl: Gouge p.64 #3, p.68 #3. Related: a 2° pitch change during speed brake extension/retraction is normal with the SBI (p.67, p.71 #27).

q: Speed brakes: may not fully extend above ___; blowback occurs above ___.
SLATS caution light coming into the break:
opts: Return flaps to previous setting and continue
Slow to and maintain below 200 KIAS; land as soon as practical

q: SLATS caution light illuminates when:
opts: Slats not in selected position, split slats, or slats selected/extended above 217 knots

q: Per IC 21/43 ASYMMETRIC FLAPS/SLATS (uncommanded roll/yaw during flap/slat transition):
opts: FLAPS/SLATS lever – Return to previous setting
expl: IC 21/43. Gouge p.7 #7 / Quizlet EP2 #7: return flaps to previous position. p.4: rapid roll during flap/slat transition = split flap/slat.

q: Why may the flap position light not show a split flap?
opts: It is disabled with weight on wheels
It is connected to the left flap only
It is powered by the non-essential AC bus
expl: Gouge p.35.

q: HYD 1 or HYD 2 failure — first consideration (gouge):
expl: Quizlet EP1 #16 / gouge p.5 #16.

q: With a HYD 2 failure you should monitor:
expl: Gouge p.59 #15, p.65; Quizlet EP1 #21.

q: With a HYD 2 pressure failure, the RAT maintains HYD 2 pressure at:
expl: Quizlet EP1 #4; gouge p.5 #4, p.62 (A), p.57.

q: The RAT deploys when HYD 2 falls below ___ psi; HYD 2 reset requires ___ psi.
expl: Gouge p.48, p.49 #27/#30, p.57. HYD 2 caution light on at 1,660 ± 110, out at 2,000 psi.

q: HYD 1 failure — what is still available for landing?
opts: Emergency gear extension, emergency flaps, and an arrested landing (all of the above)

q: HYD 1 below 1,500 psi — general services lost include:
opts: Normal gear, normal flaps/slats, normal brakes, NWS, L-bar extension, speed brakes, hook retract
expl: Gouge p.49 #37 (priority valve isolates flight controls at 1,500 psi, p.40/p.57).

q: Effect of a HYD 1 failure on the tailhook:
opts: It lowers only with RAT pressure
It can be lowered (gravity/snubber) but not raised

q: HYD 1 and HYD 2 failed, RAT working, but the aircraft is 'uncontrollable':
opts: Lower the gear with the emergency handle
Reduce airspeed below 300 KIAS and land
expl: Gouge p.59 #1, p.64 #6 — key word 'uncontrollable'.

q: The wheel brake/emergency flap accumulator provides:
opts: 10 brake applications and emergency flap extension (no slats); flaps cut off at 2,200 psi
Flap and slat extension plus 5 brake applications
expl: Gouge p.49 #31–32, p.57, p.41 (≤2,200 psi emergency flap lever has no effect).

q: Per IC 21/43 BRAKE FAILURE – ASHORE/SKID, if flyaway airspeed is NOT available, step 2 is:
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Go around (if flyaway airspeed available). Otherwise: 2. Throttle – idle 3. Brakes – release 4. Anti-skid switch – off 5. Brakes – apply gradually 6. Hook – down 7. Parking brake handle – pull. Older gouge EP 11X p.68 #5 omits throttle idle and adds 'Throttle – OFF (if departing rwy)' — older gouge, differs.

q: Per IC 21/43 BRAKE FAILURE – ASHORE/SKID, if brakes are still unavailable after applying gradually:
opts: Hook – down (if required); Parking brake handle – pull (if required)
expl: IC 21/43 steps 6–7. The older gouge has no parking-brake step.

q: Per IC 21/43 BRAKE FAILURE – AFLOAT:
opts: Throttle – idle; Parking brake handle – pull; Hook – down; Transmit
expl: IC 21/43. Not covered by the gouge (only a topic title on p.69).

q: Per IC 21/43 LOSS OF DIRECTIONAL CONTROL, if NWS failure is suspected:
expl: IC 21/43 step 6. The gouge only says 'use differential braking' (p.5 #5, p.59 #10) — older gouge, differs.

q: Per IC 21/43 LOSS OF DIRECTIONAL CONTROL, if a blown tire is suspected (no flyaway airspeed):
opts: Brakes – release; Anti-skid switch – off; Brakes – apply gradually
expl: IC 21/43 steps 3–5. Gouge: rudder as required to counter swerve, anti-skid off prior to braking (p.60 #21, p.66 #23, p.76 #21).

q: If aborting with a blown tire, set the ANTI-SKID switch ON — true or false?
expl: Quizlet EP1 #6; IC 21/43 blown tire: anti-skid switch – off.

q: Blown tire on takeoff, continuing the takeoff (gouge EP 11X):
opts: Rudder as required; do NOT reposition gear and flaps; monitor engine instruments; execute landing with blown tire procedure
expl: Gouge p.70 #11.

q: Landing with a single blown tire and no arresting gear (gouge):
expl: Gouge p.73 #31, p.76 #22; Quizlet EP2 #20.

q: Landing with dual blown tires and no arresting gear available (gouge):
opts: Consider a gear-up landing or controlled ejection

q: Short-field arrestment touchdown point when directional control is IN question:
opts: At or 50 ft prior to the gear
expl: Gouge p.73 #33, p.74 #3, p.7 #6; normal short-field arrestment: 500 ft prior.

q: Long-field arrestment (gouge 'for test only'):
opts: Hook down 1,000 ft prior; maintain directional control; release brakes as you cross the cable
Hook down 500 ft prior; brake hard
Touch down 50 ft prior to the gear
expl: Gouge p.71 #26.

q: NWS AUG goes on during taxi. You should:
opts: Press and hold the paddle switch
expl: Quizlet EP1 #25 / gouge p.6 #25.

q: Emergency (EMERG) gear extension effect on nosewheel steering:
opts: NWS works in high gain only
expl: Gouge p.3, p.69.

q: Anti-skid OFF situations (gouge '5 times'):
opts: After HYD 1 failure, before setting the parking brake after shutdown, carrier landings, SKID caution light, blown tire
Every landing, every takeoff, taxi, formation, IMC

q: HOOK warning light meaning:
opts: Hook position does not agree with the handle
Airspeed above 200 KIAS with hook down
expl: Gouge p.71 #17 (hw correction), p.44; Quizlet EP2 #33.

q: Light in the landing gear handle:
opts: Gear in transit or not in the commanded position

q: Per IC 21/43 SMOKE OR FUMES IN COCKPIT, step 1 is:
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Mask – on/tight 2. Initiate controlled descent to below 18,000 feet MSL 3. Air Flow Knob – Off. Older gouge (p.70 #12, p.75 #13) has no mask step — older gouge, differs.

q: Per IC 21/43 SMOKE OR FUMES, initiate a controlled descent to below:
expl: IC 21/43 step 2. Older gouge / Quizlet EP2 #5: 'descend below 25K' — older gouge, differs.

q: Per IC 21/43 SMOKE OR FUMES, if unable to clear smoke or unable to see, the steps are:
opts: Airspeed – reduce; warn other occupant/secure loose items; Seat – lower; MDC Firing Handle – pull
Canopy – jettison via emergency handle only
expl: IC 21/43 steps 4–7. Older gouge adds 'Visor – Down' and 'Land as soon as possible'.

q: Per IC 21/43 RAPID DECOMPRESSION:
opts: OBOGS – on and mask tight; reduce AOA
Air Flow Knob – off then on
Emergency oxygen green ring(s) – pull; OBOGS flow selector(s) – off; descend below 10,000 feet cabin altitude
expl: IC 21/43 (same three steps as ADVERSE PHYSIOLOGICAL SYMPTOMS).

q: Per IC 21/43 ADVERSE PHYSIOLOGICAL SYMPTOMS, the procedure applies if above:
expl: IC 21/43: If above 10,000 feet cabin altitude: 1. green ring(s) pull 2. OBOGS flow selector(s) off 3. descend below 10,000 ft cabin altitude. Gouge/Quizlet EP2 #1: descend below 10,000 ft cabin alt with an OBOGS failure.

q: Per IC 21/43 OXYGEN WARNING LIGHT (in flight), step 1 is:
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – set minimum 80% rpm 2. Execute Adverse Physiological Symptoms (as required). Older gouge/Quizlet EP2 #8: 'OBOGS/ANTI-G switch off', descend below 10,000 cabin alt — older gouge, differs.

q: OXYGEN warning light causes (gouge systems notes):
opts: O2 concentration below 95%, overheat above 250°F, or OXYGEN switch off
expl: Gouge p.53 #106, p.44, p.51 hw (OBOGS still works just below 95%).

q: CABIN ALT warning light procedure per the gouge (not on the IC 21/43 immediate-action list):
opts: OBOGS – on and mask tight; reduce AOA; Air Flow knob – off then on; if light remains on, descend below 25,000 ft MSL; land as soon as practical
Mask – on/tight; descend below 18,000 ft MSL
Emergency O2 green ring – pull; descend below 10,000 ft cabin altitude
expl: Gouge p.68 #1, p.74 #1, p.64 #1. Not one of the 22 IC 21/43 items — don't confuse 25,000 ft with the 10,000 ft cabin altitude of RAPID DECOMPRESSION.

q: CABIN ALT warning light illuminates at a cabin altitude above:
Canopy loss (gouge):
opts: Descend to 10,000 ft or minimum safe altitude and less than 200 KIAS

q: CANOPY caution light in flight (gouge/Quizlet EP2 #21):
expl: Gouge p.7 #21. CANOPY light + tone with canopy unlocked and power above 95% (p.4, p.53).

q: Per IC 21/43 OIL PRESS WARNING LIGHT, step 1 is:
opts: Throttle – Set and maintain 78 to 87% rpm
expl: IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – set and maintain 78 to 87% rpm 2. Minimize throttle movements. Older gouge: 'min for safe flight' (p.59 #5) or 'idle' (p.64 #10) — older gouge, differs.

q: ECA 2 caution light limits (gouge/Quizlet EP1 #7):
opts: Do not exceed 90% above 20K MSL, 95% below 20K MSL, 600°C EGT; land as soon as practical
Do not exceed 85% at any altitude

q: ACCEL caution light during descent passing 7,000 ft MSL:
opts: Steam ingestion valve closed — no effect
Expect slower engine acceleration during the approach
expl: Quizlet EP1 #3; gouge p.5 #3. p.54 #115: steam ingestion valve stuck open or initial shot-of-fuel solenoid not in commanded position.

q: LP PUMP caution light in flight:
opts: Avoid abrupt throttle movements and set minimum for flight
expl: Quizlet EP1 #10; gouge p.5 #10. Illuminates below 35 psi (p.37, p.61).

q: After the F PRESS light illuminates and you check the engine switch on, you should:
expl: Quizlet EP1 #17; gouge p.5 #17. F PRESS also illuminates 30 s after a GEN failure (boost pumps stop) (p.39, p.61).

q: MFD failure indications (gouge):
opts: Blank or blinking screen, stuck pushbutton, wrong/invalid info
expl: Gouge p.68 #4, p.74 #6, p.30; Quizlet EP2 #11.

q: Multiple MFD failures — corrective action:
opts: Display Power switch – momentarily to RESET
expl: Gouge p.76 #27, p.47 #10 (single MFD: turn it off); Quizlet EP2 #22.

q: DEU failure leaves you with which approach?
Pitot-static failure question — the instrument that still works:
expl: Gouge p.8 #27, p.64 #16; Quizlet EP2 #27. Complete pitot-static failure: lose mach/airspeed and barometric altitude, NOT vertical velocity (p.14).

q: Barometric altimeter failure (gouge):
opts: Check pitot heat; use RADALT below 5,000 ft AGL; use cabin altimeter if unpressurized
expl: Gouge p.7 #12, p.76 #24; Quizlet EP2 #12.

q: Per IC 21/43 DEPARTURE/SPIN PROCEDURE, steps 1–3 are:
opts: Throttle – MRT; speed brakes – extend; stick – full aft
Controls – neutralize/forcibly center rudder pedals; Speed brakes – retract; Throttle – idle
Rudder – full with turn needle; stick – forward; throttle – idle
expl: IC 21/43 steps 1–4 (4. check altitude, AOA, airspeed, and turn needle).

q: Upright spin recovery per IC 21/43 (AOA above 28 units):
opts: Rudder – full opposite turn needle; lateral stick – full opposite turn needle
Rudder – with turn needle; lateral stick – opposite
Rudder – full opposite turn needle; lateral stick – full WITH turn needle; longitudinal stick – neutralize
expl: IC 21/43 steps 8–10. Gouge p.25: Aileron full WITH turn needle for upright spins; p.20 #45: aileron positions reversed upright vs inverted.

q: Inverted spin recovery per IC 21/43 (AOA pegged at 0 units):
opts: Rudder – full opposite turn needle; lateral stick – full opposite turn needle; longitudinal stick – neutralize
Rudder – full opposite turn needle; lateral stick – full with turn needle
Rudder – with turn needle; lateral stick – with turn needle
expl: IC 21/43 steps 5–7. Gouge p.25: Aileron full OPPOSITE turn needle for inverted spins.

q: Inverted spin characteristics (gouge):
opts: 0 units indicated AOA, negative G, turn needle in direction of spin

q: Per IC 21/43, if out of control passing through ___ AGL: Eject.
expl: IC 21/43 DEPARTURE/SPIN step 13.

q: Per IC 21/43 DEPARTURE/SPIN, neutralize lateral stick when recovery is indicated or airspeed increases through:
expl: IC 21/43 step 11; then 12. Rudder pedals – smoothly center.

q: Midair with your wingman — per the gouge, the right answer is:
opts: Join up on the other aircraft to inspect
Have someone else (not the aircraft you hit) give you a visual inspection; don't have the wingman join up

q: In ejection situations the gouge says to:
Engine EGT limits (gouge): max at idle / ground start / airstart:
expl: Gouge p.37, p.56. MRT 610°C (30 min/hr); transient 645°C (<20 s).
